findings.result: The frozen HTML/text identify arXiv:2610.21411v2 [cs.AI], 16 Oct 2026 and the exact title. ACM 2018/Woodstock/placeholder DOI/ISBN/CCS are template artifacts; notes correctly reject them as real publication metadata. Frozen HTML spells the second author Zhaojiacheng Zhou. The separate v1=2026-10-15 claim has no independent submission-history evidence in these ten refs; see nonblocking limits.

Equations 1–11 and Algorithm 1 support the notes: configured roles and legal candidates; artifact-grounded routing; selected expert gets task/prior artifacts/feedback; no requirement that a bounded selector invent a whole plan; screen-pass bypasses LLM re-review; escalation yields an independent generative assessment with possible acceptance or repair feedback; repair is generative and re-enters screening. The notes do not infer missing context closure, recovery, effect fencing or dynamic expert creation.

C.3 states 150 sampled MATH, MBPP+ and I3 instances, seed 42 stratified; API-Bank 150 episodes / 445 prediction points. API accuracy is strict per prediction point while tokens, calls, latency and estimated dollar costs are per episode. MBPP+ is EvalPlus base plus extended pass@1; I3 is label accuracy, not open-ended research quality. Main token and call metrics cover generative LLMs and omit decision-model/SLM usage. Notes preserve these differences.

Read all Table 1 values. Ours-vs-LAS token savings round to DeepSeek 17.5%,20.8%,39.4%,54.6%; GPT-5 21.8%,12.7%,38.5%,38.6%. Across displayed ACC values, largest loss is 1.34 percentage points (GPT-5 MBPP+). Seven of eight latency comparisons improve; GPT-5 MATH 30.04/25.91−1 is about +15.94%. Notes accurately describe these as author point estimates, preserve the exception and higher MetaGPT DeepSeek I3 accuracy, and do not claim statistical noninferiority or universal quality improvement.

Read all Table 2 settings. Content-Blind masks substantive outputs in router input while retaining task/legal actions/metadata/inter-expert communication; it is not removal of all expert execution context. I3 accuracy difference 75.33−57.33=18.00pp; API 66.29−57.30=8.99pp. Notes explicitly flag the manuscript introduction's inconsistent 9.02pp statement. Heuristic/Rule quality losses and Planner-Replan worse outcomes are retained; multiple trajectory/call differences preclude a pure router-speed conclusion.

Read all Tables 3–4 and §§5.4/C.3. Notes correctly retain injected task-relevant intermediate errors, task-level accuracy/ASR, stronger but more costly MAD, cascade vs LLM-review token savings (10138−8657)/10138=14.61% and (12430−9736)/12430=21.67%, Jev clean FPR4.00/6.67 versus LLM1.33/5.33, attack TPR95.33/91.33 versus LLM96.67/92.00, and SLM low-FPR/poor-TPR tradeoff. ASR definition/denominator and exact injection implementation are not fully specified; notes do not fabricate them. One minus reported Jev TPR gives 4.67%/8.67% screening misses on corrupted cases, not a universal final-task failure probability.

C.2 equations 12–15 use completed screening operations, including revised-artifact checks; rho=pi*r+(1−pi)*f; checkpoint cost CJ+rho*CL beats CL only if CJ<(1−rho)*CL. Error-pass is unconditional pi*(1−r). Natural artifact-error prevalence is not estimated by controlled injection ratios. Notes preserve these assumptions and the distinction from full-workflow routing/generation/repair/repeated-check cost.

Read Appendix A, all Table 5/B.1–B.2 values and C.3. Higher call allowances improve listed ACC without always exhausting the budget; API resource trends are nonmonotonic. Heterogeneous backbones improve I3 but degrade API and increase tokens. Main I3 vs B=6 discrepancy is not silently explained away. Predefined pool, artifact-quality distribution, unspecified prompts/default controls/role pool/checkpoint frequency/repeated seeds/CIs/pricing classes and exact deployment model are correctly treated as limitations rather than filled in.
